4._section_summary: This Procedure describes translation/back-translation of the BAS-2 into Persian and data collection between December 2014 and June 2015 at seven large universities in Tehran. Participants were university students who completed a paper-and-pencil survey in classroom settings; the BAS-2 was included and counterbalanced with other measures. 5.evidence_source: The factor structure of the BAS-2 was examined using a principal-axis exploratory factor analysis (EFA) with quartimax rotation (because of the expectation of a single factor; see Swami & Ng, 2015; Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015b).
5._section_summary: This section describes statistical analyses for the BAS-2: a principal-axis EFA with quartimax rotation was performed (with eigenvalues >1, scree plot, and parallel analysis used for retention) and the EFA was conducted separately for women and men. Ten independent t-tests compared BAS-2 items between genders, an additional t-test compared total BAS-2 scores, and Pearson correlations were used to examine associations among body appreciation, self-esteem, life satisfaction, BMI, and age. No explicit study numbering, sample sizes, demographic details, or BMI assessment methods are reported in this section.

6._section_summary: This section reports EFA results for the male subsample of a BAS-2 instrument: KMO = 0.86 and Bartlett's test significant (–2(45) = 2550.95, p < .001). Parallel analysis and inspection of the scree plot indicated a single-factor solution explaining 49.9% of variance (eigenvalues 4.98 and 1.06 reported), all ten items loaded on the primary factor, and internal consistency was acceptable in men (Cronbach's α = .89). The section refers to a 'male subsample' but does not label any study as 'Study 1' or similar.
